name: Rivanna Trail
description: Explore the Rivanna Trail and its connecting trails around Charlottesville. The Rivanna Trails Foundation maintains maps, trail guidance, and opportunities to help care for the network.

visitor_info.label: Dogs
visitor_info.value: Dogs must be leashed.

visitor_info.label: Trail use
visitor_info.value: Stay on the trail and respect adjacent private property. No motorized vehicles, camping or loitering.

name: Ragged Mountain
description: Wooded walking trails around Ragged Mountain Reservoir. Check the City’s current construction information before heading toward the shoreline or dam.

visitor_info.label: Hours
visitor_info.value: Daily, 7 a.m. to sunset.

visitor_info.label: Dogs
visitor_info.value: No pets; service dogs are welcome.

visitor_info.label: Water access
visitor_info.value: No swimming.

visitor_info.label: Construction
visitor_info.value: The City reports shoreline closures in sections and closure of the upper parking lot; use the lower Heyward lot and follow posted detours.

name: Saunders–Monticello
description: A winding path and connecting woodland trails near Monticello. The trail manager’s guide includes parking, hours, trail maps, and access rules.

visitor_info.label: Hours
visitor_info.value: Sunrise to sunset; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and during unsafe weather. Winter ice can delay opening.

visitor_info.label: Dogs
visitor_info.value: Leashed dogs are welcome on trails and boardwalks.

visitor_info.label: Bikes
visitor_info.value: No e-bikes. Other bicycles: 10 mph maximum and yield to pedestrians. Boardwalks closed to bikes when wet.

visitor_info.label: Winter access
visitor_info.value: Loggers Alley closes where it crosses ski slopes during ski season. Other steep trails can be hazardous with ice and snow; check the current guide.

name: James Monroe’s Highland
area: James Monroe Parkway, southeast of Charlottesville
description: Highland’s Rustic Trails cross woods and pastures beside James Monroe’s historic home. Choose gentle pasture loops or the steeper Mountain Trail; use the official map to plan your walk.

info_sources.label: Highland trail hours and visitor information

visitor_info.label: Hours
visitor_info.value: Daily, 9:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m., weather permitting; no trail entry after 3:30 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year’s Day.

visitor_info.label: Admission
visitor_info.value: Trails are free; check in at the Museum Shop on arrival. Tickets are required for the historic core.

visitor_info.label: Dogs
visitor_info.value: No pets except on designated Dog Days; service animals are welcome. Check Highland’s events calendar for Dog Days.

visitor_info.label: Trail use
visitor_info.value: No bicycles, horses or motorized vehicles. Stay on marked trails and respect private property.

visitor_info.label: Wet weather
visitor_info.value: Highland asks visitors to wait 24 hours for each inch of rainfall before using the trails. Bring drinking water; none is available on the trails.

bounds_source.description: Envelope of seven existing Strava-derived Highland-area trail features, padded 0.001 degrees; compared visually with the official 2023 trail map. Context extent only, not an access boundary or a route refresh.

name: Fortune’s Cove Preserve
description: Steep woodland trails and rocky overlooks above Lovingston. The official map marks a 5.1-mile yellow loop and a shorter 3.7-mile white loop that avoids the highest climbs.

info_sources.label: TNC preserve information and access updates

visitor_info.label: Hours
visitor_info.value: Open daily, dawn to dusk, year-round.

visitor_info.label: Dogs
visitor_info.value: No pets; service animals are welcome.

visitor_info.label: Trail use
visitor_info.value: No bikes, horses, camping or fires. Stay on designated trails and respect adjoining private property.

visitor_info.label: Difficulty
visitor_info.value: The upper loop is strenuous, with about 1,500 feet of climbing; allow around four hours. The white shortcut reduces the distance and climbing.

visitor_info.label: Facilities
visitor_info.value: Gravel parking and a map kiosk at the entrance; no restrooms. Bring water.

visitor_info.label: Road access
visitor_info.value: TNC reports storm erosion on the entrance road; use caution, especially without a high-clearance vehicle. Check the official page before visiting.

bounds_source.description: Extracted official GeoPDF trail extent, padded 0.001 degrees; context envelope, not a preserve boundary.

name: Lake Anna State Park
description: Woodland and lakeshore trails with easy and moderate routes, historic sites and lake views. The park offers more than 15 miles of trails; consult the official map for each trail’s uses and difficulty.
map_note: DCR’s alert, checked Nov. 3, 2026, lists a Nov. 2–3 closure for resource management. Check current park alerts before visiting.

info_sources.label: DCR Lake Anna visitor information and alerts

visitor_info.label: Hours
visitor_info.value: Normally dawn to dusk for day use; current closures take priority. The park lists a 5 a.m. gate opening.

visitor_info.label: Dogs
visitor_info.value: Keep pets on a leash no longer than 6 feet or confined; do not leave them unattended.

visitor_info.label: Trail use
visitor_info.value: Hiking throughout; bikes and horses only on designated multi-use trails. Hikers yield to horses; cyclists yield to horses and hikers.

visitor_info.label: Parking
visitor_info.value: Daily parking fees apply. The park may reach capacity on weekends and holidays, so entry is not guaranteed.
